[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Recursive Queries** [CF 932B · Recursive Queries](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/932/B){rating="1300"}

$g$ depends only on $x$, and $x$ lives in a small fixed universe $[1, 10^6]$. So compute $g(x)$ for **every** $x$ once (a digit-product recursion, memoised bottom-up is not even needed — each $x$ settles in a few steps), then the question "how many $x \in [l,r]$ have $g(x)=k$" is a *range count over the value axis*, exactly the 1D prefix sum of @sec-pref — just with one prefix table per answer $k$. That is a two-dimensional table $\text{pref}[k][i] = \#\{x \le i : g(x)=k\}$, and each query is one subtraction $\text{pref}[k][r] - \text{pref}[k][l-1]$ in $O(1)$.

[Solved in full in @sec-nd-p1-rq.]{.card-link}
